q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT s1.bar AS bar1, s2.bar AS bar2 FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.beer = s2.beer AND s1.bar <> s2.bar WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s3 WHERE s3.bar = s1.bar AND NOT s3.beer IN (SELECT s4.beer FROM serves AS s4 WHERE s4.bar = s2.bar)) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s5 WHERE s5.bar = s2.bar AND NOT s5.beer IN (SELECT s6.beer FROM serves AS s6 WHERE s6.bar = s1.bar))

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they use different approaches to check the existence of beers served by specific bars. Q1 uses a NOT EXISTS subquery to check if a beer is not served by a bar, while Q2 uses a NOT IN subquery to check if a beer is not in the list of beers served by another bar. These approaches can yield different results if the subqueries return NULL values.
